title: Thirty-Second Handle Count
description: Players count how many clean moves of a given type they make in 30 seconds, then try to beat their own score — a self-measured skill test.

content.objective: Measure and improve ball-handling speed and control with a simple, repeatable personal test.
content.setup: Players spread out with a ball each; the coach runs a stopwatch.
content.organization: Whole group tests together; players record their own scores.
instructions: Test 1: crossovers in 30 seconds; count each clean change of hand.
Test 3: weak-hand pound dribbles in 30 seconds.
A move only counts if the ball stays below the waist and under control.
Repeat the tests the following week and compare.
coachingPoints: Quality first: a sloppy move does not count.
commonMistakes: Counting moves with the ball above the waist.
Standing up as fatigue sets in.
Losing the ball and giving up the round.
content.safety: Personal spaces at least two metres apart; stop a test if a ball rolls into someone's space.
progressions: Add a 'with eyes closed for 5 seconds' challenge for advanced players.
regressions: Count only the strong hand at first.
variations: Team total challenge against another team.
successCriteria: Beats the previous week's score on at least one test.
No counted move made above the waist.
content.gameApplication: Tracking scores turns ball-handling homework into visible progress players will practise on their own.
